I have two proposals for improvements to Voat which I believe would help immensely, unless I'm overlooking an exploitable flaw:

(Sorry beforehand to Putt, these are wishful thinking. I am an IT person, and I know implementing new code isn't quick or easy!)

1) Aggregate the Information. This constantly driven media tidbit style of information delivery is helpful for everyday people to share real stories, but postings can be spammed and upvoated from shill accounts, and the substantive matter is never aggregated per topic, leaving crucial info to be lost or "memory holed" if not laboriously archived and saved into directories on your PC. I know of the post "save" feature, but it require you to browse pages of saved posts to find that one piece of info you were looking for.

Is there any form of tagging or otherwise grouping all of the pertinent PROVEN information on a subject - whether it's climate hoax/racism hoaxes/pizza gate/wiki leaks/epstein/etc - into a repository where it can be kept more continuous and therefore impactful? I'm thinking differently than subverses here, a single repository for factual information on a given topic - not just posts of news articles, but dissected facts - can be made quickly available to the eye and mind without stumbling through posts.

2) Apply to all users a new Validity Score value. In addition to the upvoat, downvoat system we have in place, which seeks to allow site users to "self regulate" the popularity of a submitted subject or comment - Voat needs a per user Validity Score.

The Validity Score works in tandem with upvoats, downvoats, CCP, SCP by allowing users to mark a post as VALID (TRUE) or FAKE (FALSE). The user who posted the link/discussion has those positive/negative Validity Score values added to his account, following them around for the rest of their Voat career - displayed to anyone who hovers his article/user name.

We've seen it too many times before, someone rushes in with a twitter or facebook post, and it is discovered to be fake news about 3 hours after people have re-shared the story or wasted valuable time talking about the fake subject.

In this case, users can go back to the post, and reduce the users Validity Score because that user shared a non-verified, sensationalist piece of news. The Validity Score doesn't punish people by reduce their ability to post, it punishes users with a low Validity Score by keeping other users skeptic of the information they post - a "hardening" of the community, if you will, against disinfo.

Users who regularly share verifiably true stories will be rewarded (by other users who appreciate not having their time wasted) with a higher Validity Score, meaning the stories this users posts will most likely be researched and TRUE stories.

Last, but not least, Validity Score points are kept in the users history, and ALL USERS are allowed to see specifically which submissions/comments/stories a given user has scored as Valid. This will help other users to identify shills who will try to give their shill accounts a high Validity Score through circular upvoating via their sock puppet accounts. This also helps to identify spiteful people/trolls who aren't necessarily shills - if you see a user who regularly marks TRUE posts by a specific user as FALSE as a form of revenge because his feelings got hurt in an argument, the entire Voat community will know that user is a troll, and his posts will be taken with a couple more grains of salt next go round. There's many benefits to having a Validity Score System in line with the upvoat/downvoat system when it comes to identifying problem accounts, shills, and trolls.
